entries.value: NSW Health reported (19 Oct 2026) 1,180 presentations to NSW emergency departments associated with peptide use between 1 July 2025 and 30 September 2026. The release does not break this figure down by peptide. The release names GHK-Cu among the peptides that products may claim to contain and states: "None of these peptides are currently approved in Australia for any purpose."

No entry naming GHK-Cu was found in the Poisons Standard (October 2026; F2026L01327; in force from 1 October 2026). This page does not state a schedule for it. Schedule 4 also contains class entries, including one for COPPER COMPOUNDS for human use (with exceptions); this page does not assess whether any class entry applies to a GHK-Cu product. Not being named does not mean a product is unscheduled or may lawfully be supplied, and the NSW release states that GHK-Cu is not approved in Australia for any purpose.

GHK-Cu is not FDA-approved as a drug. Topical formulations are widely available as cosmetic products. Injectable forms are classified as research peptides. The compound's natural occurrence in human plasma provides inherent safety rationale but does not constitute regulatory approval.

GHK-Cu is not FDA-approved as a drug. Topical formulations are widely available as cosmetic products. Injectable forms are classified as research peptides. The compound's natural occurrence in human plasma provides inherent safety rationale but does not constitute regulatory approval.

GHK-Cu is not an FDA-approved drug. FDA's list of bulk drug substances nominated for compounding under section 503A (document updated 14 May 2026) places "GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration)" in Category 1, "Bulk Drug Substances Under Evaluation". FDA explains that GHK-Cu was removed from Category 1 on 22 April 2026 after the nominations were withdrawn. It was added back for non-injectable routes after one nominator clarified on 5 May 2026 that it meant to withdraw only the injectable route. Under FDA's interim policy, FDA generally does not intend to take action against 503A compounding with a Category 1 substance while the nomination is evaluated, if other conditions are met. This is enforcement discretion, not placement on the 503A bulks list and not an approval.

**Injectable routes:** FDA's page "Certain Bulk Drug Substances for Use in Compounding that May Present Significant Safety Risks" (content current as of 22 April 2026) lists "GHK-Cu (for injectable routes of administration)" under "Bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn". FDA's text reads: "Compounded injectable drugs containing GHK-Cu may pose risk for immunogenicity due to the potential for aggregation and peptide-related impurities. There are limited data in humans to inform safety-related considerations."

**Advisory committee:** FDA states that it intends to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) "before the end of February 2027" on whether GHK-Cu could be included on the 503A bulks list. The PCAC meeting page (content current as of 15 April 2026) lists GHK-Cu on the agenda with LL-37, dihexa acetate, melanotan II and PEG-MGF, and says the meeting time and location will be scheduled. No date was posted as of 22 Oct 2026.
None of these listings is an approval. Advisory committee advice is non-binding, and Peptidemap does not predict the outcome.
